SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we promote healthy relationships in the community?

1. explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HEALTHY RELATIONSHIPS - EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION - NEGOTIATION SKILLS - EMPATHY
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: HEALTHY RELATIONSHIPS - EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION - NEGOTIATION SKILLS - EMPATHY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy” around your school. (skill: explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we promote healthy relationships in the community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Healthy relationships - effective communication - negotiation skills - empathy means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
